A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main texts, figures, table, equations and appendices support comparison, and relocated theoretical material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 Section 6 and Figures 3–6 report original experiments on S5 state tracking, MQAR, WikiText-103 perplexity and WikiText-2 inference latency.

after.justification: V2 Section 4 and Figures 3–6 retain these original experiments and add Mamba perplexity and latency results.

M1.justification: V1 Section 6 specifies causal self-attention for both aggregation and inference. V2 Section 3.4 specifies bidirectional attention for aggregation while retaining causal inference. This changes the stated aggregation procedure within the same scan architecture; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use S5 state tracking, uniformly sampled MQAR, WikiText-103 language modeling and WikiText-2 latency evaluation. No additional dataset, task or distinct test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: V2 adds Mamba to the WikiText-103 perplexity and WikiText-2 latency comparisons in Figures 5–6, which previously compared Transformer-PSM with GPT-2. Mamba already appeared in S5 and MQAR; comparator membership in those experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added Mamba comparisons introduce specified configurations: 130M parameters, width 768 and 10 training epochs for language modeling, and four layers with width 256 for latency. Existing data-generation rules, evaluation lengths, metrics and chunk-size sweeps are retained. Newly disclosed configurations for existing experiments do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The S5 length-generalization analysis, MQAR chunk-size comparison and WikiText-103 chunk-size sensitivity study are retained. The reorganized appendices contain theoretical material, not new ablations, robustness tests or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added Mamba results use the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds Mamba perplexity of 24.7 and reported average latency of approximately 0.006 seconds per token. The stated Transformer-PSM perplexities of 24.12 and 22.45, GPT-2 perplexity of 22.28, and S5/MQAR findings are retained. These additions do not establish a same-setting improvement in Transformer-PSM.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 changes the stated module-depth requirement from polylogarithmic depth to O(1) and corrects the chunk count from t/c to n/c. The principal affine-scan results, streaming-equivalence proofs and computational-complexity derivations are retained, largely through relocation into the expanded appendices.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the unification of efficient sequence models through prefix scans, generalization to non-associative aggregation, efficient streaming inference and favorable empirical capabilities. V2's numbered contributions restate these claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: V1 Section 7 explicitly states that the framework neither automatically generates new models nor predicts their relative practical performance. V2's merged discussion and conclusion omit these substantive limitations. Interpretations of the retained experimental findings are otherwise largely unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit embedding and module specification, previously omitted widths, head counts and layer allocations, and a reproducibility statement with a code-release link. These expand documentation. The newly stated latency-model width of 768 also exposes an inconsistency with the retained equal-parameter claim against a width-256 GPT-2 baseline.

R1.justification: V2 discusses concurrent Log-linear Attention as fitting the proposed framework and adds references to recurrent fast-weight programmers, DeltaProduct, Fixed-point RNNs and RWKV-7. These update the research context while retaining the central positioning of prefix scannability.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: technical preliminaries and extended theoretical discussions move to appendices, the main theory is condensed, Transformer-PSM receives a dedicated subsection, contributions become an explicit list, and discussion and conclusion are merged. Numerous explanatory passages are rewritten.

P2.justification: The manuscript adopts a conference layout with extensively resized and relocated displays. Algorithms change from full-width stacks to paired columns, and the S5/MQAR plots become a side-by-side pair. Figures 5–6 add Mamba series, Table 1 removes its Mamba-2 row, and an appendix contents page is added.

improvement.justification: The dedicated model specification, additional implementation details, code-release information and Mamba comparisons modestly improve clarity, reproducibility documentation and empirical context. These gains are tempered by removal of explicit limitations and the unresolved latency-comparison inconsistency between the stated model widths and equal-parameter claim. The central evidence and proofs remain largely unchanged.
